d: A very common interview pattern asking for the K largest/smallest elements.
c: Kth Largest Element in an Array

p: To find the Top K Largest elements, maintain a Min-Heap of size K. Why a Min-Heap for Largest? Because the root (smallest in the heap) acts as a threshold. If a new element is larger than the root, we pop the root and push the new element.
1. Insert first K elements into Min-Heap.
2. For remaining elements, if `element > heap[0]`, `heappop` and `heappush(element)`.
3. The heap now contains the Top K largest.

def findKthLargest(nums, k):
  minHeap = nums[:k]
  heapq.heapify(minHeap)
  
  for num in nums[k:]:
    if num > minHeap[0]:
      heapq.heappop(minHeap)
      heapq.heappush(minHeap, num)
      
  return minHeap[0]
Time: O(N log K). Better than O(N log N) sorting! Space: O(K) for the heap.

Array: [3, 1, 5, 12, 2, 11], K=3
Min-Heap maintains top 3 largest elements:
Insert 3: [3]
Insert 1: [1, 3] -> [3] (pop 1)
...
Final Heap: [5, 11, 12]
